title: Research: independent COPY floor for arbitrary one-column P112 corrections
body:
An arbitrary free correction on one P112 column can invalidate the earlier rank-eight-per-child argument. This independent proof still bounds the **complete COPY power bill** when any two original coordinate terms and that correction are mixed by any `GL(3,C)` change of factors. All **28 coordinate pairs, 112 singleton sites, arbitrary complex amplitudes and every subset of the 52 odd neighbors** are covered; transposition gives one-row corrections. Six original terms remain fixed.

The three replacement ranks satisfy `sum r_j^q >= 2*8^q` for every `0<q<=1`. The complete COPY sum has sharp floor **64**, and the complete power bill has sharp floor **8*8^q**, attained by identity mixing for every allowed correction. The proof accounts for the pure correction factor through lower envelopes `(8,8,0)`, `(6,6,6)` or `(6,6,4)` and uses the coupled inverse-factor identity. Added physical overhead is optimistically zero for this COPY screen; width, normalization, multiplicity and separate charging remain fixed.

Only `research/p112-column-correction-floor/` is added (14 files): written proof, explicit task/source/replay metadata, complete certificate, two geometry representations, exact Gaussian-rational full-decoder examples and controls.

Validation:

- Full registered Python 3.12 replay and all seven test groups pass. The second engine independently constructs Euclidean roots and a full Gram-derived binary code, importing no primary or predecessor geometry.
- Complete coverage: 140 support strata, 71,540 character evaluations, **15,680 full odd-neighborhood survivor slices**, 15,680 singleton erasures and 700 pairings. Thirteen full nine-term fixtures check **163,072 entries**, projection branches, correction charges and factor-matrix ranks.
- Read-only isolated optimized Python 3.14 replay has identical canonical receipt `6d621ea5ffffc4079cc50a8bf4a0e4d83305ec48ce78b7d95e844da97a4c0627`; all runtime input bytes remain unchanged. Semantic mutations, real source/receipt corruption, source pins, package selection and clean patch application pass.

**Overlap and attribution:** commdata2338's PR1375 supplies the small-rectangle theorem, support/erasure method and 24-row boundary; Cinna Davis's PR1373 supplies the three-active branch for pair (4,6); Arham Tahir's PR1331 supplies the earlier handoff. The final refresh found Hanson Sun/bbMisk's PR1432 (`4bcc49e3f4041018b0607da46a87d8928a6e0fd0`), which already proves the fixed 24-row case and the same `(7,8,7)` example, and PR1460 (`8d53667d9bb09d9b1ffb0f865b5c8dc230eb02f6`), an independent arbitrary-rectangle compensation bound at (4,6). Those findings are credited; this package provides an independently derived all-pair one-column proof and complete certificate. No pending theorem or code is assumed. Discussion1360's all-nine-factor singleton completion and the newer two-column claim are also recorded. The final overlap snapshot covered 824 open PRs and 159 discussion records, fully paginated.

One OS draw selected `complex-mechanisms / complex-masked-decoder`, nonce `149d7583c4efedede03fc432c003699f`, scope key `2a6f2c726b78f9ae7d26`, priority revision 2. The required complex-field starting example passed. [Discussion1434](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1434) records the refined scope and handoff. Research and refreshed submission base are `410026dc5513b87db92ae98571d1d5984c69a983`, with both live inputs unchanged.

Reproduce:

```sh
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-column-correction-floor
```

**Limits:** this package does not prove a floor for general two-sided rectangles, more mixed coordinates, other punctures or shared COPY billing. No physical word, frame/restoration schedule, owner/hosting admission, native run, selected cold replay, precision/tape, all-size compiler or analytic transfer is supplied. The universal argument is written, not proof-assistant checked. No new supplier or improved κ. Hosted CI and maintainer review remain separate from local validation.

Retains credit to Mihir Srivastava/PR845, DreamingOfClouds/PR717/446/595, GamingPuzzled/PR620, themilkman216/PR968 and woklerx/PR1077/1180. New work by Gareth Davidson (@bitplane), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematics, both implementations, tests and writing; Apache-2.0. No subagents or independent human review.
